title: UK CPI, January 2027 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the FIRST of the two annual weight updates, not the resolution of the electricity weight three lanes point at it
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukjanuary2027, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 42,071 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Consumer price inflation, UK: January 2027', 'Provisional release date: 17 February 2027 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', and carries the accredited-official-statistics kitemark. Filed estimate on ONS's own Provisional label, on this lane's no-self-confirm limit, and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Canonical file written by the uk-cpi-2027-02-17 lane 2026-09-09 after reading all three proposals for this id (from ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25, uk-cpi-2027-05-19 and uk-cpi-2027-11-17)
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 FROM THREE PROPOSALS, ALL OF WHICH SHARE ONE FACTUAL ERROR THIS LANE CORRECTS. All three diarised this date as the venue where the 2027 CPI electricity weight (ONS series CJXA) resolves, turning two sibling ledgers' size bands into numbers; FT-uk-cpi-2027-11-17-3 registers a CJXA prediction with score-by 2027-02-17. IT DOES NOT RESOLVE HERE. ONS runs a 'double update' methodology introduced in 2017 (Consumer price inflation, updating weights: 2026, released 16 March 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09): a FIRST update of weights for the January indices only, price-updated to December of the prior year, and a SECOND update for the February-to-December indices, price-updated to January of the current year. The published annex (Annex A Tables W1-W3, 2026 edition, xlsx parsed direct) carries BOTH columns per year since 2017 — CJXA 2024 Jan 22.2747 vs Feb-Dec 23.3142, 2025 Jan 18.9060 vs Feb-Dec 19.1488, 2026 Jan 19.7795 vs Feb-Dec 20.6065 — and the MM23 series CJXA publishes the FEBRUARY-TO-DECEMBER value in 6 of 6 years where the two differ (2017, 2019, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026), never the January one. So the weight that scales the 2027-04-01 VAT reversion (April and October 2027 both sit in the Feb-Dec window) is published with the FEBRUARY 2027 index on 2027-03-24 and documented in the updating-weights article, which has landed in MARCH in all ten years 2017-2026 and never in February. The annual BASKET update is in the same February print, not this one: the January 2026 bulletin says verbatim 'The second update will be introduced, along with the usual basket update, with the February indices released on 25 March 2026.' WHAT THIS PRINT DOES CARRY, honestly: the January-only weight vintage (a real number, running 1.3-4.7% below the operative Feb-Dec weight in the three unrounded years), the January Ofgem cap step, and the January sales month — January is the only calendar month with a negative mean m/m in D7BT (-0.473%, 2015-2026). The VAT SIDE IS CLEAN: both December 2026 and January 2027 sit inside the SI 2026/987 zero-rate window (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31), so this m/m carries no tax content — and BOTH price-update reference months (Dec 2026 for stage one, Jan 2027 for stage two) are inside it too, which is why the uk-cpi-2027-11-17 lane's exact 5/105 cancellation survives even though the stage it cited was the wrong one. Tiered LOW on the standing measurement: symbols [], no UK listing, gilt or sterling instrument on this calendar, whose tracked universe is eight US mega-caps. Corridor is dense and American: this 02:00 ET print shares 2027-02-17 with the VIX February settlement (confirmed) and with the January FOMC minutes at 14:00 ET — a date proposed in this PR as fomc-minutes-2027-02-17, verified from the Fed's own calendar where the decision-day-plus-21 rule reproduced 5 of 5 in 2026. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
